identity.title: The NADHX epimerase NAXE governs PARP1-DNA retention to maintain poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation homeostasis.

content.abstract: PARP1 is a crucial enzyme involved in DNA-damage repair and other biological processes through poly(ADP-ribose) modification (PARylation), but persistent activation can trigger parthanatos. Despite extensive research, the precise mechanisms governing PARP1 activity remain elusive. Here, through multiple CRISPR-Cas9 screens, we identified NAXE, an NADH hydrate (NADHX) epimerase, as a key regulator of PARP1 activity homeostasis. We show that NADHX inhibits PARP1-DNA binding, while NAXE lowers NADHX levels to promote PARP1 recruitment and DNA repair. PARP1 activation, in turn, induces PARylation that binds and inhibits NAXE, forming a negative feedback loop that restrains PARP1 aberrant activation. Notably, knockout of NAXE in mice and C. elegans disrupts PARylation homeostasis, leading to sustained DNA damage and PARP1 activation, ultimately resulting in parthanatos-driven catastrophic neural injury. These findings uncover a metabolite-mediated feedback mechanism that preserves PARylation homeostasis and highlight NAXE as a potential therapeutic target in PARP1-related neurological disorders.
